title: Symmetry-ordered section specialization of the canonical projection mate
statement:
Symmetry-ordered section specialization of the canonical projection mate. In the existing RingedTensorCorner, RingedTensorModel and RingedTensorEdge interfaces, with TensorConstraints and the normalized comparison predicates of lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition, assert exactly the following independent part of its coherence calculation:

theorem ringedProjectionSectionSpecialization
    {X : RingedTensorCorner.{u, w}} (a : RingedTensorModel X)
    (tx : TensorConstraints X a) :
    (∀ (W : RingedTensorCorner.{u, w}) (i : RingedTensorEdge W X)
          (p : RingedTensorEdge X W) (d : RingedTensorModel W) (s : Section i p),
        ∃ (tw : TensorConstraints W d) (l : p.left ⋙ i.left ≅ 𝟭 X.mateDerived),
          s.Normalized l ∧ ∀ M V : X.mateDerived,
            sectionComposite i p a d tx tw l M V = 𝟙 (X.tensor.obj (M, V)))

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), 0DV0 (categories.tex, lemma-compose-counits); formal tensor-associativity and section specialization of the canonical projection mate

proof.text: Take the canonical constraints on W and the right-ordered section comparison supplied by sectionProjectionComparison. Expand the two leftProjection maps. Naturality moves the first outside symmetry past the section inverse. Functoriality combines the two adjacent middle symmetries, and involutivity cancels them. Naturality of the right section comparison and of the final symmetry leaves the right-ordered section projection. Its equation cancels the section inverse and section comparison. Involutivity on X cancels the two outside symmetries.
